title: NEW EMUCOREX UPDATE RELEASED:PLAYSTATION 2 EMULATOR FOR ANDROID MALI GPU TEST
summary: A long Resident Evil 4 field test of EmuCoreX on a OnePlus 10R, documenting a MediaTek Dimensity 8100-Max and Mali-G610 platform instead of relying on the more common Adreno path.

blocks.text: EMU GAMES dedicates the recording to one named workload and one fully identified device: Resident Evil 4 on a OnePlus 10R with Dimensity 8100-Max, Mali-G610 MC6, 8 GB RAM, Android 15 and on-screen touch controls. The description says the footage examines FPS, stability and graphics quality across real gameplay. That combination makes the video valuable as a Mali-specific field report; it shows the kind of non-Adreno configuration for which custom Turnip assumptions are irrelevant and the system graphics stack matters more.

The title associates the result with a newer EmuCoreX build, but it does not list the renderer, internal resolution, exact build identifier, game region, sustained temperature or frame-time method. A single Resident Evil 4 run cannot represent the full PS2 library, and an FPS overlay cannot by itself prove correct pacing or rendering. Treat it as evidence for this OnePlus and game pairing, then repeat the same scene after a cold start and after thermal saturation before drawing a device-wide conclusion.
